quests.question: Don't give up ___ your dreams just because things got difficult.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to stop believing in or pursuing something.
quests.explanation: 'Give up on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to stop believing in or pursuing something.

quests.question: I don't know how she puts up ___ his constant complaining.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to tolerate something unpleasant.
quests.explanation: 'Put up with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to tolerate something unpleasant.

quests.question: He has a bad habit of looking down ___ people who didn't go to college.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to consider someone inferior.
quests.explanation: 'Look down on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to consider someone inferior.

quests.question: The team needs to come up ___ a better solution by Friday.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to think of or produce an idea.
quests.explanation: 'Come up with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to think of or produce an idea.

quests.question: He actually thought he could get away ___ cheating on the exam.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to avoid punishment for something wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Get away with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to avoid punishment for wrongdoing.

quests.question: We're about to run out ___ time, so let's wrap this up.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to have no more of something left.
quests.explanation: 'Run out of' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to have none of something left.

quests.question: I finally have a free weekend to catch up ___ some reading.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to do something you've fallen behind on.
quests.explanation: 'Catch up on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to do something you've fallen behind on.

quests.question: It's hard to keep up ___ all the new technology trends.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to stay at the same pace as something changing quickly.
quests.explanation: 'Keep up with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to stay at the same pace as something moving or changing.

quests.question: Despite her doubts, she decided to go through ___ the wedding.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to complete a plan despite hesitation.
quests.explanation: 'Go through with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to complete something despite doubts.

quests.question: At the last minute, he decided to back out ___ the deal entirely.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to withdraw from an agreement.
quests.explanation: 'Back out of' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to withdraw from an agreement or commitment.

quests.question: The doctor advised him to cut down ___ sugar and caffeine.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to reduce the amount of something.
quests.explanation: 'Cut down on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to reduce the amount of something.

quests.question: The new manager wants to do away ___ unnecessary paperwork.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to eliminate something entirely.
quests.explanation: 'Do away with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to eliminate or get rid of something.

quests.question: I wanted to follow up ___ your question about the refund policy.
quests.hint: This is a single formal word meaning 'concerning' or 'about'.
quests.explanation: 'Regarding' is a formal single-word preposition meaning 'concerning' or 'about', common in professional writing.

quests.question: ___ your recent email, I can confirm the shipment has been sent.
quests.hint: This is a formal multiword phrase pointing back to something already mentioned, like an email.
quests.explanation: 'With reference to' is a formal multiword phrase used to point back to something previously mentioned, such as an email.

quests.question: The professor made no mention ___ the exam changes during today's lecture.
quests.hint: This is the standard fixed word after the noun 'mention'; a common learner error uses a different word here.
quests.explanation: 'Mention of' is the correct fixed form; 'mention about' is a common but incorrect error many learners make.

quests.question: He's fallen behind ___ his mortgage payments for the third month in a row.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to fail to keep up with a financial obligation.
quests.explanation: 'Fall behind on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to fail to keep up with a payment or schedule.

quests.question: She always follows through ___ her promises, no matter how small.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to complete what you said you would do.
quests.explanation: 'Follow through on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to complete a commitment you made.

quests.question: I think I'm coming down ___ something — I've had a headache all day.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to be starting to feel ill.
quests.explanation: 'Come down with' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to become ill with a minor sickness.

quests.question: It's important to hold on ___ your core values, even under pressure.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to keep believing in something firmly.
quests.explanation: 'Hold on to' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to keep or maintain something firmly, like a value or belief.

quests.question: At some point, you have to let go ___ the past and move forward.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to stop holding onto something emotionally.
quests.explanation: 'Let go of' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to release something emotionally, like the past.

quests.question: Don't miss out ___ this limited-time offer.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to fail to take advantage of an opportunity.
quests.explanation: 'Miss out on' is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to fail to take advantage of an opportunity.

quests.question: ___ the delay, we would like to offer you a full refund.
quests.hint: This introduces the topic of the message, not its cause.
quests.explanation: 'Regarding' introduces the topic of a message, distinct from 'because of', which would state a cause.

quests.question: The contract will be renewed automatically ___ that both parties agree in writing.
quests.hint: This introduces a condition that must be met, meaning 'as long as'.
quests.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a required condition, meaning 'as long as' or 'on the condition that'.

quests.question: Approval was granted ___ condition that all safety measures be followed.
quests.hint: This is the fixed word that always begins this particular conditional phrase.
quests.explanation: 'On condition that' is a fixed formal phrase meaning 'provided that'; 'on' is the word that always begins it.

quests.question: After years of struggling, the small bakery finally started to catch up ___ its bigger competitors.
quests.hint: This is the fixed phrasal verb for reaching the same level as someone else, taught earlier in this course.
quests.explanation: 'Catch up with' fits reaching the same level as competitors, distinct from 'catch up on', which is used for tasks like reading.

quests.question: He's been trying to cut down ___ his spending since losing his job.
quests.hint: This is the same fixed phrasal verb taught earlier in this course, for reducing something.
quests.explanation: 'Cut down on' returns here, describing an effort to reduce spending.

quests.question: She finally decided to back out ___ the risky investment before it was too late.
quests.hint: This is the same fixed phrasal verb taught earlier in this course, for withdrawing from something.
quests.explanation: 'Back out of' fits again, describing a withdrawal from a risky commitment.

quests.question: Despite the setbacks, the founders never gave up ___ their vision for the company.
quests.hint: This is the same fixed phrasal verb taught earlier in this course, for abandoning a belief.
quests.explanation: 'Give up on' closes this idea, describing founders who never abandoned their vision.

quests.question: We've been able to expand our services this year, ___ your continued support.
quests.hint: This credits a positive cause for a good outcome, as taught earlier in this course.
quests.explanation: 'Thanks to' credits a positive cause for a good outcome, the same idiom taught earlier in this course.

quests.question: The company's success can be attributed ___ its unwavering focus on customer service.
quests.hint: This links an outcome back to its cause, as taught earlier in this course.
quests.explanation: 'Attributed to' closes this unit, linking the company's success back to its cause.
